title: FCDO Research Advisory Group 2026: Part-Time Remote Opportunity for Senior Global Research and Policy Experts
summary: The FCDO Research Advisory Group (RAG) is seeking experienced experts to join its advisory group and provide independent scientific and research advice to the UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO) . This is a senior-level, part-time advisory opportunity for individuals with substantial expertise in areas such as health, agriculture, climate, energy, water, economic growth, humanitarian affairs, education, governance, conflict, social development, data for development, big data and artificial intelligence . Members will contribute strategic advice on FCDO s research priorities, funding portfolio, evidence use, research quality, value for money, emerging global challenges and connections with the wider UK and international research community. The position is remote, part-time and unremunerated , although FCDO will reimburse reasonable economy travel and incidental expenses associated with the role. About the FCDO Research Advisory Group The FCDO Research Advisory Group was established in 2022 to provide strategic guidance, rapid insight and independent challenge to FCDO s research funding portfolio. The Group supports the work of the FCDO Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA) , who is also the Director of the Research and Evidence Division. Its role is to help assure the quality, relevance and appropriateness of FCDO s research portfolio . The Group brings together experts with thematic and geographic knowledge covering a wide range of global development and international policy issues. Its areas of expertise include: Health Agriculture Climate Energy Water Economic growth Humanitarian affairs Education Governance Conflict Social development Data for development Big data Artificial intelligence Innovation and related research areas Members are expected to contribute their expertise while also engaging with issues that extend beyond their own individual academic discipline. What Is the Role of an FCDO Research Advisory Group Member? Members provide independent scientific and research advice to FCDO . The role is not simply about advising on an individual s specialist field. Members are appointed in a personal capacity , meaning they serve as independent experts rather than representatives of their employer, profession, institution or an interest group. Members are also expected to contribute across the Group s broader agenda. Their responsibilities include providing insight into how research and evidence can support international development and wider foreign policy objectives. Key Responsibilities 1. Advising on FCDO Research Priorities Members will contribute to discussions concerning: FCDO s research priorities Research activities The relationship between FCDO research and the wider UK science base Connections with international research communities Emerging areas where additional research may be required Their advice can help FCDO consider whether its research portfolio is addressing important global challenges and research needs. 2. Supporting Evidence-Informed Policy A central responsibility of the Group is helping ensure that FCDO policy is informed by the best available research and evidence . Members may therefore be asked to consider the quality, relevance and usefulness of research being used to inform policy. This requires an understanding of how research can be translated into practical policy and development impact. 3. Reviewing Research Programme Effectiveness Members will comment on the: Effectiveness of research programmes Value for money of research investments Funding mechanisms for research and development Performance and relevance of research activities This means applicants should be able to engage with questions concerning not only academic quality but also the practical impact and effectiveness of research funding. 4. Advising on the Research Portfolio Members will help assess the overall balance and adequacy of FCDO s research portfolio. This includes identifying: Research gaps Areas requiring greater attention Areas that may deserve less emphasis Emerging research priorities Opportunities for strengthening the overall portfolio Members therefore need to be able to think beyond individual research projects and consider research strategically at portfolio level. 5. Horizon-Scanning and Scenario Planning The Group also participates in horizon-scanning and long-range scenario planning . This involves considering emerging global challenges and developments that could have implications for research, international development and policy. Experts should therefore be comfortable thinking about future trends and possible challenges rather than focusing exclusively on current issues. 6. Connecting FCDO With Specialist Expertise Members can provide advice and connections to specialist expertise across: The UK research community International research institutions Academic networks Relevant specialist fields Global research communities Their networks and understanding of the international research environment can therefore contribute to the Group s advisory role. 7. Emergency Response and Disaster Preparedness Where required, members may also provide advice on scientific inputs to FCDO s emergency response and disaster preparedness . This responsibility highlights the importance of having experts who can apply research and evidence to rapidly changing international situations. Time Commitment The position is designed to be compatible with other professional responsibilities. Members are expected to participate in: Four meetings per year Approximately 2.5 to 3 hours per meeting Approximately 2 to 3 hours of reading and preparation for each meeting Occasional additional meetings or direct engagement when FCDO requires specific expert advice Meeting papers are expected to be circulated approximately one week before each meeting , allowing members time to review the material and prepare. Meeting dates will be confirmed as far in advance as possible. There may also be occasional ad hoc requests for expert input between scheduled meetings. Length of Appointment The appointment is for: Three years The term is renewable once , with a maximum of: Two terms This means a member may potentially serve for up to six years if their appointment is renewed. Remuneration and Expenses The position is unremunerated . Members do not receive a salary for serving on the Research Advisory Group. However, the information provided states that reasonable travel expenses and incidental expenses will be reimbursed by FCDO . Where travel is required, the stated provision is for economy travel . Applicants should therefore understand that this is a professional advisory appointment rather than a salaried part-time employment position. Employment Arrangement The position is listed as: Employment Type: Part Time Location: Remote The remote nature of the role means that members can participate without being based at a particular FCDO office. However, applicants should take into account that the role may involve meetings or activities requiring travel, with reasonable eligible travel and incidental expenses reimbursed according to the stated arrangements. Who Is FCDO Looking For? The Research Advisory Group is seeking individuals with a combination of subject-matter expertise, senior professional experience, international perspective and the ability to provide independent advice . The selection criteria emphasize several important characteristics. Selection Criteria 1. Relevant Thematic Expertise Applicants should have expertise, skills and experience in a relevant thematic area. The identified thematic areas include: Health Agriculture Climate Energy Water Growth Humanitarian affairs Education Governance Conflict Social development Data for development Applicants whose expertise relates to broader research, innovation, technology or evidence issues may also be relevant where their expertise connects with the Group s agenda. 2. Seniority and International Reputation The Group is looking for individuals with an appropriate level of seniority and international reputation . This is therefore a senior expert/advisory appointment rather than an entry-level opportunity. Applicants should be able to demonstrate a substantial record of expertise and contribution in their relevant field. 3. Familiarity With Government Processes Applicants should have familiarity with: Government processes Key government policies Policy development The relationship between research and government decision-making Experience of working with government, public institutions or policy environments can therefore be relevant to the role. 4. Independence and Fairness Members must be committed to a fair and independent process . Because the Group provides independent advice, members are expected to approach issues objectively and contribute professional judgement without allowing personal or institutional interests to determine their advice. 5. Breadth of Academic Discipline The selection process values breadth across academic disciplines. Applicants should have an understanding of transdisciplinary approaches to global challenges . This is important because many of the issues addressed by FCDO cannot be examined through one discipline alone. For example, challenges involving climate, health, development, conflict or technology can involve multiple scientific, social, economic and policy perspectives. 6. International and Global Perspective Applicants should have an international and global perspective. Particular emphasis is placed on: Capacity strengthening in the Global South Translation of research into impact Research partnerships Working with international partners Understanding how research can contribute to development outcomes Experience working across countries, regions or international research networks may therefore be relevant. FCDO Research and Development Context The Research Advisory Group operates within a broader FCDO research and development environment. Following publication of the Global Research and Technology Development (GRTD) Approach Paper , launch of the GRTD website and confirmation of long-term funding, FCDO s research and development portfolio now includes: A large Official Development Assistance (ODA) programme A smaller but growing non-ODA portfolio The non-ODA component is focused on broader foreign policy and national security objectives . This means the Group s work extends across a diverse research portfolio involving development, international policy and other strategic priorities. Appointment in a Personal Capacity A significant condition of the appointment is that members serve in their personal capacity . They are not appointed as representatives of: Their employer Their university Their profession An interest group Another organization Members are also expected to contribute across the full agenda of the Research Advisory Group , rather than restricting their contribution exclusively to their own academic discipline. This makes breadth of perspective and the ability to engage with multidisciplinary issues particularly important. Principles and Standards Expected of Members Members must abide by the Seven Principles of Public Life , commonly known as the Nolan Principles . They are also expected to take account of the Government Chief Scientific Adviser (GCSA) s Principles of Scientific Advice to Government . These expectations reinforce the importance of: Independence Integrity Evidence Professional conduct Responsible advisory practice Transparency around interests Declaration of Interests Successful members must complete a declaration of interests when appointed. The declaration must also be kept up to date throughout their appointment. This is important because members may be involved in discussions concerning research programmes, funding mechanisms and research priorities. Applicants should therefore be prepared to disclose relevant interests and maintain accurate declarations during their term. Confidentiality and Information Security Members will have responsibilities concerning FCDO information and documentation. FCDO documents and information used by the Group are Official UK Government papers and must not be shared outside the Group. Members will therefore be responsible for safeguarding: FCDO documents Research-related information Meeting papers Advisory materials Other official information provided to the Group Applicants should be comfortable working within appropriate confidentiality and information-security requirements. Selection Process The selection process involves several stages. Step 1: Submit an Application Interested applicants are required to submit: A CV An expression of interest The application should demonstrate how the applicant s experience, expertise and perspective correspond to the requirements of the Research Advisory Group. Step 2: Shortlisting Applications will be reviewed and suitable candidates will be shortlisted. The selection criteria include thematic expertise, seniority, international reputation, government familiarity, independence, multidisciplinary perspective and international experience. Step 3: Panel Interview Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a panel interview. The panel will be led by the Co-Chairs and will include the: Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA), and/or Deputy Chief Scientific Adviser (Deputy CSA) Candidates should therefore be prepared to discuss their expertise, experience, understanding of research-policy relationships and ability to contribute to the Group s broader agenda. Application Deadline The stated application deadline is: 30 September at 11:59 PM UK time Important Application Form Instruction Because this is a part-time and unremunerated position , applicants are specifically instructed to enter: N/A in both the: Salary expectations field Notice period field Applicants should follow this instruction rather than entering a salary expectation or employment notice period. How to Apply Applicants interested in joining the FCDO Research Advisory Group should prepare a strong CV and expression of interest addressing their suitability for the position. The application should demonstrate relevant evidence of: Thematic expertise Senior professional experience International experience or perspective Understanding of government and policy processes Independent and fair judgement Multidisciplinary or transdisciplinary experience Research translation and impact Capacity strengthening, particularly in the Global South Relevant professional and academic networks Ability to contribute to the Group beyond a narrow disciplinary area Applicants should also ensure that the salary expectations and notice period fields contain N/A , as instructed in the vacancy announcement. Apply Here Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity Member, FCDO Research Advisory Group Organization Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO) Role Type Part-time advisory appointment Location Remote Appointment Length 3 years Renewal Renewable once Maximum Terms 2 terms Meetings 4 per year Meeting Duration 2.5–3 hours Preparation 2–3 hours per meeting Additional Commitment Occasional ad hoc input Remuneration Unremunerated Travel Reasonable economy travel reimbursed Incidental Expenses Reimbursed by FCDO Main Focus Research, evidence, science advice and research funding Key Expertise Health, agriculture, climate, energy, water, growth, humanitarian affairs, education, governance, conflict, social development and data for development Application CV and expression of interest Selection Shortlisting followed by panel interview Interview Panel Co-Chairs and CSA and/or Deputy CSA Deadline 30 September at 11:59 PM UK time Salary Expectations Field Enter N/A Notice Period Field Enter N/A Important Considerations Before Applying Potential applicants should consider the following before submitting an application: 1. It is a senior-level position The selection criteria specifically mention seniority and international reputation. 2. It is unpaid The role is unremunerated, although reasonable travel and incidental expenses are reimbursed. 3. It requires ongoing commitment There are four meetings each year, preparation for each meeting and occasional additional requests for advice. 4. Independence is important Members serve in their personal capacity and must support a fair and independent process. 5. Confidentiality is required Members will have responsibilities for safeguarding Official UK Government documents and information. 6. Multidisciplinary thinking is expected Members are expected to contribute across the Group s agenda rather than only discussing their own specialist area. 7. International experience is relevant The selection criteria specifically refer to an international and global perspective and capacity strengthening in the Global South. Read Full Details about this Job opportunity HERE Conclusion The Member, FCDO Research Advisory Group opportunity provides experienced research and policy experts with the opportunity to contribute independent scientific and research advice to the UK s Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office. The Group plays a strategic role in examining FCDO s research priorities, assessing research programmes and funding mechanisms, identifying gaps, considering emerging global challenges and strengthening the connection between research evidence and policy. The position is particularly relevant to senior experts with substantial thematic expertise, international perspective, familiarity with government processes, multidisciplinary experience and a strong understanding of how research can be translated into policy and practical impact . Members will serve for an initial three-year term, renewable once, and will participate in four meetings each year alongside occasional additional advisory activities. The position is remote and part-time but is unremunerated , with reasonable economy travel and incidental expenses reimbursed by FCDO. Applicants should submit a CV and expression of interest and be prepared for a panel interview if shortlisted. The stated deadline is 30 September at 11:59 PM UK time . Applicants should also enter N/A in the salary expectations and notice period fields because the position is part-time and unremunerated. title: Morgan Stanley 2027 Investment Management Sophomore Summer Analyst Program in New York: Private Credit & Equity Internship
summary: Are you an undergraduate student interested in investment management, private credit, private equity, financial analysis, valuation, and private-market investing ? Morgan Stanley is offering a 10-week 2027 Investment Management Sophomore Summer Analyst Program – Private Credit Equity in New York, United States . The program is designed for undergraduate students who want to gain practical exposure to the investment management industry and develop skills that are relevant to careers in private markets and investment analysis. Participants will join Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s Tactical Value team , where they will work alongside investment professionals on research, financial analysis, investment opportunities, portfolio monitoring, and other activities connected to the investment decision-making process. The application deadline is September 25, 2026, at 11:55 PM Eastern Time (ET) , while applicants must complete their HireVue digital questionnaire by September 27, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET . About Morgan Stanley Investment Management Morgan Stanley Investment Management (MSIM), together with its investment advisory affiliates, operates as part of Morgan Stanley s global investment management platform. According to the opportunity description, MSIM has more than 1,300 investment professionals worldwide and $2 trillion in assets under management or supervision as of June 30, 2026 . Morgan Stanley describes its investment management business as focused on providing long-term investment performance, client service, and investment management solutions to a diverse range of clients, including governments, institutions, corporations, and individual investors. Morgan Stanley also maintains a dedicated careers platform for students, graduates, and experienced professionals, with opportunities across investment banking, investment management, wealth management, technology, and other areas. Opportunity Overview The 2027 Investment Management Sophomore Summer Analyst Program – Private Credit Equity is a 10-week summer internship beginning in June 2027 . The program combines formal training with practical experience inside a specific Investment Management team. The structure includes: One week of training Nine weeks working within the assigned Investment Management team During the program, Summer Analysts are expected to gain exposure to the professional environment of Morgan Stanley and perform work that is similar in nature to the responsibilities of a full-time Analyst. The program is designed as a learning and development opportunity. Morgan Stanley specifically notes that participation in this role does not necessarily correlate with full-time opportunities within the firm . Program Location Location: New York, United States The position is based within Morgan Stanley s Investment Management business in New York. Morgan Stanley maintains a global presence and states that its employees work across 41 countries , with opportunities available to students and graduates in different regions. Team: Tactical Value Successful participants will join the Tactical Value team . The Tactical Value team focuses on identifying and evaluating opportunistic investment opportunities across private markets . This provides Summer Analysts with an opportunity to learn about how investment professionals examine potential investments, conduct research, assess companies and industries, evaluate financial information, and contribute to the investment process. Participants can expect exposure to areas including: Private-market investing Private credit Private equity Investment research Financial analysis Company analysis Industry research Financial forecasting Valuation Portfolio analysis Investment due diligence Investment memoranda Market developments Portfolio-company monitoring Project management This combination of research, quantitative analysis, qualitative assessment, and investment-related work can provide students with a practical introduction to the processes used in private-market investing. What Will Summer Analysts Do? The internship involves a range of investment-related responsibilities. 1. Conduct Investment Due Diligence Summer Analysts will work with senior members of the Fund to conduct due diligence on potential investment opportunities. Due diligence involves gathering and analyzing information about a prospective investment so that investment professionals can better understand its financial position, business model, industry, risks, opportunities, and overall investment characteristics. Students may therefore have opportunities to develop their ability to: Research companies Examine financial information Investigate industries and markets Identify important investment considerations Organize information for senior investment professionals Support the evaluation of prospective investments 2. Coordinate With Advisors and Consultants Participants may also coordinate with external advisors and consultants involved in investment due diligence. This responsibility can expose interns to the collaborative nature of investment transactions, where investment teams may work with professionals from different areas to obtain specialized information and analysis. Strong communication, organization, attention to detail, and professionalism are therefore important. 3. Build Financial Forecasts and Valuation Models One of the more analytical components of the internship involves helping construct company financial forecasts and valuation models . This can involve working with financial information to understand a company s historical performance and develop assumptions about potential future performance. Students interested in investment management can gain practical experience in areas such as: Financial forecasting Revenue and expense analysis Financial statement analysis Valuation Investment assumptions Financial modeling Quantitative analysis These are important skills for professionals working in investment management and private markets. 4. Support Other Investment-Related Activities Summer Analysts may also assist with other investment-related activities. The opportunity description specifically mentions tasks such as: Tracking prospective investment deals Assisting with confidentiality agreements Supporting investment-related projects Organizing information associated with potential investments Helping investment professionals with ongoing analysis This means the internship is not limited to financial modeling. Participants may be exposed to the broader workflow involved in evaluating and progressing investment opportunities. 5. Contribute to Investment Memoranda Participants will also have the opportunity to contribute to investment memoranda relating to investment opportunities. An investment memorandum typically brings together relevant research and analysis so that investment professionals can evaluate a potential transaction or investment opportunity. This responsibility can help students develop their ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally. Skills that may be developed include: Written communication Investment research Data interpretation Company analysis Industry analysis Presentation of findings Attention to detail Business writing 6. Monitor Existing Portfolio Companies The role also involves monitoring the performance of existing portfolio companies. This can help interns understand that investment management does not end when an investment is made. Investment professionals may continue to monitor companies, markets, financial performance, and other factors affecting their investments. Participants can therefore gain insight into portfolio management and ongoing investment analysis. 7. Follow Financial and Economic Developments Summer Analysts will also be expected to keep current with market developments. This includes following developments such as: Changes in the economy Financial-market movements New investment products Developments affecting private markets Broader market trends Developing this habit can help students understand how economic and market developments can affect investment decisions. Skills You Can Develop Through the Program The internship is designed to help participants develop a broad set of professional and technical skills. Financial and Investment Skills Participants can gain exposure to: Financial modeling Company valuation Investment research Due diligence Portfolio analysis Private-market investing Financial forecasting Investment evaluation Research and Analytical Skills The role can also strengthen: Quantitative analysis Qualitative company research Industry research Problem-solving Critical thinking Attention to detail Economic and market analysis Communication Skills Because participants will work with investment professionals and potentially interact with advisors and consultants, communication is an important component of the role. The program specifically highlights opportunities to develop: Public speaking Written communication Presentation skills Professional communication Company and industry analysis Project Management Participants will also have opportunities to develop project-management skills, including the ability to: Manage competing priorities Organize research Track prospective deals Meet deadlines Work independently Collaborate with colleagues Present information effectively Who Should Apply? The program is particularly relevant to undergraduate students who are interested in careers involving: Investment management Private equity Private credit Asset management Financial analysis Investment banking Corporate finance Valuation Private markets Portfolio management Financial research Applicants should have a genuine interest in investing and be prepared to demonstrate analytical ability, academic achievement, communication skills, teamwork, and motivation. You do not necessarily need to have already worked in private equity or private credit. The program itself is structured as a learning and development experience for students. Key Candidate Qualities Morgan Stanley is looking for candidates who demonstrate several professional qualities. Exceptional Academic Performance Applicants should demonstrate strong academic performance. Academic achievement can be particularly relevant for competitive investment-management internships because students are expected to analyze complex information and learn technical concepts quickly. Strong Communication Skills Candidates should have strong verbal and written communication skills. This is important because the role involves research, presentations, investment memoranda, collaboration, and communication with other professionals. Teamwork Applicants should be comfortable working as part of a team. Investment management involves collaboration between investment professionals, analysts, advisors, consultants, and other stakeholders. Independence and Initiative Morgan Stanley is also looking for self-starters who can work independently. Candidates should be able to take responsibility for assigned work, organize their tasks, identify information they need, and make progress without requiring constant supervision. Motivation and Results Orientation Applicants should demonstrate that they are driven, highly motivated, and focused on producing quality results. Organization and Time Management Because Summer Analysts may work on multiple projects and competing priorities, strong organizational and time-management skills are important. Problem-Solving Ability The role requires an analytical and detail-oriented mindset. Candidates should be able to examine information, identify important issues, and contribute to solving investment-related problems. Interest in Investing A clear interest in investing is specifically listed as a job requirement. Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate why they are interested in investment management and, particularly, private-market investing. Program Structure The program will run for approximately 10 weeks beginning in June 2027 . The structure is: Week 1 — Training Participants begin with formal training intended to provide foundational knowledge and skills needed for the Investment Management environment. Weeks 2–10 — Team Placement The remaining nine weeks involve working within a specific Investment Management team. For this opportunity, participants will join the Tactical Value team and gain hands-on exposure to research, financial analysis, investment-related projects, and the investment decision-making process. Compensation The stated expected base pay rate is: $36.06 per hour at the commencement of employment. Morgan Stanley notes that base pay is determined on an individualized basis and forms only part of the overall compensation package. Depending on the position, compensation may also include other forms of compensation and benefits, such as: Incentive compensation Discretionary bonuses Commission earnings where applicable Other short- and long-term incentive packages Morgan Stanley-sponsored benefit programs The exact compensation package should be confirmed through the official employment documentation and applicable terms for the position. Application Process Candidates must complete the application process through Morgan Stanley. The stated process requires applicants to: Step 1: Submit Your Resume Candidates must submit their resume through the Morgan Stanley careers website. Morgan Stanley maintains an online careers platform specifically for students, graduates, and experienced professionals. Step 2: Complete the HireVue Questionnaire Applicants must also complete the required HireVue digital questionnaire . Completing the questionnaire by the specified deadline is necessary for the application to be considered. Step 3: Submit Before the Deadline Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis , meaning candidates are encouraged to apply early rather than waiting until the final day. The position may close when it is filled or when the stated application deadline is reached. Important Application Deadlines Applicants should pay attention to two separate deadlines . Application Deadline September 25, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET This is the deadline stated for submitting the application. HireVue Deadline September 27, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET Applicants must complete their HireVue responses by this deadline. Because the application is reviewed on a rolling basis, students interested in the opportunity should consider submitting their application as early as possible. What Should Applicants Highlight in Their Resume? Students applying for this opportunity should make sure their resume clearly demonstrates the skills Morgan Stanley identifies in the job description. Relevant areas to highlight include: Strong academic performance Financial or investment-related coursework Finance clubs or investment societies Business or economics projects Financial modeling experience Excel proficiency Data analysis Research experience Leadership experience Teamwork Public speaking Presentation experience Project management Entrepreneurial activities Relevant internships Investment-related personal projects Applicants who do not have formal investment experience can still demonstrate relevant skills through academic projects, student organizations, research, competitions, leadership activities, or other analytical experiences. The Tactical Value team focuses on opportunistic investment opportunities across private markets . Private-market investing differs from publicly traded-market investing because investment opportunities can involve privately held companies, private credit arrangements, and other investments that are not necessarily traded on public stock exchanges. Working within this environment can expose students to the process of identifying potential opportunities, researching companies, analyzing financial information, assessing valuations, conducting due diligence, and monitoring investments. The experience described in the position therefore combines several areas of investment work rather than focusing exclusively on one technical function. Why This Internship Can Be Valuable for Students Interested in Finance The program provides exposure to several fundamental areas of investment management within a major global financial-services organization. Rather than being limited to classroom learning, participants are expected to work on actual research and investment-related activities, including financial forecasting, valuation, due diligence, investment memoranda, portfolio monitoring, and market research. The program can therefore help students understand how investment professionals evaluate opportunities and make decisions based on financial, company, industry, and market information. Morgan Stanley also states that its student and graduate opportunities are intended to provide opportunities for talented students and recent graduates to develop their careers within the firm. Important Things Applicants Should Know Before applying, candidates should keep the following points in mind: The position is a summer internship , not a permanent job. It is based in New York . Applicants must be pursuing a Bachelor s degree . Applicants must graduate between December 2028 and June 2029 . The program lasts 10 weeks . The program begins with one week of training . title: Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027: Up to £70,000 for Experienced Researchers in Any Discipline
summary: The Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 provide funding for experienced researchers who need dedicated time to complete a programme of original research. The scheme is particularly aimed at researchers whose routine teaching and administrative responsibilities have limited their ability to undertake research in recent years. The fellowship offers up to £70,000 and can support research periods lasting between 3 and 24 months . Researchers from a wide range of academic disciplines can apply, making this an opportunity for established scholars seeking protected time to develop and complete substantial research projects. About the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships The Research Fellowships are offered by the Leverhulme Trust , a UK charitable organisation that supports research and education. The fellowship is designed around a specific challenge faced by many experienced academics: although they may have strong research ideas and established research records, their ability to conduct research can be restricted by teaching, administration and other routine institutional responsibilities. The programme therefore provides financial support that can enable successful applicants to devote a significant period of time to their research. The Trust gives particular priority to applicants whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly affected their capacity to conduct research during the three years before applying . This makes the fellowship especially relevant to experienced researchers who can demonstrate that institutional responsibilities have prevented them from giving sufficient attention to an important original research programme. Fellowship Value Successful applicants can receive funding of up to: £70,000 The maximum value gives researchers substantial flexibility to structure an appropriate period of research leave and cover eligible costs associated with undertaking the proposed research. Applicants should nevertheless ensure that their requested budget is appropriate to the scale and requirements of their proposed project rather than simply requesting the maximum amount available. Duration of the Fellowship Research Fellowships can be held for: A minimum of 3 months Up to a maximum of 24 months The duration should correspond to the amount of dedicated research time genuinely required to complete the proposed programme. A project requiring a shorter period of concentrated research may therefore be proposed for a shorter fellowship, while a more substantial programme may require a longer period, subject to the scheme s conditions and assessment. Who Is the Fellowship Designed For? The Research Fellowships are intended for experienced researchers who want to complete a defined piece or programme of original research. The scheme is particularly relevant to researchers who: Have an established research background. Have developed an original research project that requires dedicated time to complete. Have been unable to devote sufficient time to research because of routine academic responsibilities. Have significant teaching commitments. Have substantial administrative responsibilities within their institution. Can demonstrate that these responsibilities have affected their research activity during the three years preceding the application. Are able to undertake the proposed research within the fellowship period. The Trust s emphasis on the impact of teaching and administration means that applicants should clearly explain how their professional responsibilities have constrained their research time and why the fellowship would make a meaningful difference. Research in Any Discipline One of the notable features of the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowship is its broad disciplinary scope. The opportunity is available to researchers working across disciplines rather than being restricted to a single academic field. Depending on the nature of the proposed project, this can include research areas within fields such as: Humanities Social sciences Arts and related disciplines Natural sciences Other eligible academic research fields The breadth of the scheme means that the quality and originality of the proposed research, together with the applicant s experience and eligibility, are important considerations. Applicants should consult the official scheme guidance carefully to determine whether their particular discipline and research proposal satisfy the Trust s requirements. Why the Fellowship Is Important for Experienced Researchers Academic researchers often have responsibilities extending well beyond conducting research. Teaching, student supervision, administration, committee responsibilities, institutional projects and other duties can substantially reduce the amount of time available for original research. The Leverhulme Research Fellowship is structured to address this problem by providing support for a period in which an experienced researcher can concentrate on a specific research programme. For an applicant, the fellowship may therefore provide an opportunity to: Create dedicated research time The fellowship can help an experienced researcher obtain a sustained period away from routine responsibilities so that they can concentrate on their research. Complete an existing research programme Researchers who have already developed a substantial body of work but have struggled to bring it to completion may use the fellowship period to make significant progress. Develop original research The scheme is intended for original research, making the research question, methodology and anticipated contribution important elements of an application. Advance an established research career A successful fellowship can provide researchers with additional time and resources to develop significant scholarly work. Address research interruptions caused by academic duties Researchers whose teaching and administrative workload has reduced their research capacity can explain this context as part of their application. Priority for Researchers Affected by Teaching and Administrative Duties A particularly important feature of this fellowship is the Trust s stated priority for applicants whose research has been affected by routine institutional responsibilities. The Trust specifically indicates that priority will be given to applicants whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly impacted their ability to undertake research during the three years before the application . This means applicants should pay close attention to explaining their circumstances. Rather than simply stating that they are busy, applicants should demonstrate the relationship between their professional workload and their reduced research activity. For example, an applicant may need to explain: The nature of their teaching responsibilities. The extent of their administrative workload. How these responsibilities have affected their available research time. The period over which the impact occurred. How dedicated fellowship time would allow them to complete the proposed research. The purpose should be to establish a clear connection between the applicant s current circumstances and the need for the fellowship. What Type of Research Can Be Proposed? The fellowship is intended to support a piece or programme of original research . Consequently, applicants should have a clearly defined research objective rather than presenting a general desire to undertake academic work. A strong proposal should communicate: The central research question or problem. The significance of the research. The originality of the proposed work. The approach or methodology to be used. The work that will be undertaken during the fellowship. The expected scholarly contribution. Why the proposed fellowship period is necessary. How the research will progress during the requested period. The research programme should also be realistically structured around the amount of time and funding requested. Internationally Focused Projects The fellowship information also contains guidance concerning projects with an international focus . Researchers whose proposed work involves international subjects, locations, sources, collaborations or comparative research should carefully review the Trust s specific guidance on projects with an international focus before submitting an application. This is particularly important for researchers whose projects extend beyond the UK or involve research activities in multiple countries. Applicants should make sure that the international dimension of their proposal is clearly justified by the research itself and that all relevant eligibility and funding conditions are satisfied. Application Preparation The Leverhulme Trust advises prospective applicants to read the available information before beginning the application. The Trust has provided Application Help Notes 2027 to assist researchers in preparing their submissions. The guidance should be reviewed carefully because it contains information about the requirements and information applicants need to prepare. Applicants should ideally begin preparation well before the closing date, allowing enough time to develop their research proposal, assemble supporting information and review their application before submission. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the Leverhulme Grant System . Prospective applicants should: Review the Research Fellowships information provided by the Leverhulme Trust. Read the Application Help Notes 2027 . Develop a clearly defined original research programme. Confirm that they meet the fellowship s eligibility requirements. Consider the appropriate duration of the proposed fellowship. Prepare the information and supporting material required by the application system. Prepare a realistic funding request, taking into account the maximum fellowship value. Submit the completed application through the Leverhulme Grant System before the deadline. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit, particularly where institutional approval or additional information may be required. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline for the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 is: 5 November 2026 Applicants should ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated closing date and should check the official application system for any submission-time requirements. Funding Amount and Duration at a Glance Feature Details Fellowship Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 Maximum value £70,000 Fellowship duration 3 to 24 months Research area Any discipline, subject to scheme eligibility Target applicants Experienced researchers Particular priority Researchers whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly affected research during the previous three years Research focus Original research Deadline 5 November 2026 Application system Leverhulme Grant System What Applicants Should Emphasise Applicants should ensure that their proposal presents a convincing and coherent explanation of the research they intend to undertake. Several areas deserve particular attention. 1. Explain the originality of the research The application should make clear what is new about the proposed research and what contribution it is expected to make. 2. Demonstrate research experience Because the fellowship is intended for experienced researchers, applicants should present their relevant research background and demonstrate their ability to undertake the proposed work. 3. Explain the need for dedicated research time Applicants should clearly explain why the research cannot easily be completed alongside their existing teaching and administrative responsibilities. 4. Address the three-year context Researchers who have been significantly affected by teaching and administrative responsibilities should clearly explain how those duties have constrained their research activities during the relevant three-year period. 5. Develop a realistic timetable The proposed research should be achievable within the requested fellowship period. Applicants should demonstrate how the available research time will be used. 6. Prepare an appropriate budget Although the maximum award is £70,000, applicants should request an amount that is justified by the needs of their specific research programme. Research Fellowship Application Strategy A prospective applicant can strengthen the preparation process by treating the application as a coherent research case rather than simply a request for funding. The application should connect four central elements: Research problem → Original contribution → Need for dedicated time → Achievable research programme The research problem establishes what the applicant wants to investigate. The originality explains why the research matters academically. The explanation of the applicant s workload establishes why dedicated fellowship time is necessary. Finally, the research plan demonstrates that the proposed work can realistically be completed during the fellowship. This structure can help ensure that the application remains focused and that the need for fellowship support is clearly communicated. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is designed for experienced researchers . The information provided by the Leverhulme Trust does not describe the fellowship as a general scholarship for undergraduate or newly enrolled students. Applicants should therefore assess their level of research experience and their ability to demonstrate a substantive programme of original research. The Trust s emphasis on applicants affected by teaching and administrative responsibilities also means that the fellowship is particularly relevant to established researchers working within academic or research institutions. Who Is Not the Main Target of the Fellowship? Based on the stated purpose of the scheme, this opportunity is not primarily presented as a general funding programme for: Undergraduate students. Students seeking tuition funding. Applicants without an established research background. Individuals seeking general professional development funding. title: EBRD Internship 2026 in Brussels: Apply for a 6-Month Intern Position in Corporate Strategy
summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is inviting applications for an Intern position based in Brussels, Belgium , offering an opportunity for qualified graduates and early-career professionals to gain practical experience within an international financial institution. The six-month internship is situated within the Corporate Strategy Division and will involve work related to European Union policies and initiatives, institutional communications, policy engagement, events, meetings, research, and coordination. This EBRD internship provides an opportunity for an individual with an academic degree and some professional working experience to contribute to the work of the Bank s EU Representative Office while developing professional experience in an international and multicultural environment. The position may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in European Union affairs, international development, public policy, international organisations, communications, sustainability, finance, and institutional relations . Overview of the EBRD Internship Opportunity The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is recruiting an Intern to support its team in Brussels. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and contribute to a range of policy, communication, event, meeting, administrative, and coordination activities. According to the vacancy announcement, the internship has a duration of six months and is based in Brussels, Belgium. Key Opportunity Details Organisation: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) Position: Intern Division: Corporate Strategy Location: Brussels, Belgium Office Country: Belgium Office City: Brussels Contract Type: Internship Contract Length: 6 months Requisition ID: 37050 Posting Date: 11 September 2026 Application Deadline: 25 September 2026 The vacancy is designed for an individual who can support the Brussels-based team across policy engagement, communications, events, meetings, outreach, and coordination activities. About the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is an international financial institution that works across regions in which it invests. The organisation describes its approach as agile and innovative and highlights the opportunity for employees to work with experts from a wide range of professional sectors. Working at the EBRD can expose interns and other employees to professionals operating across areas including finance, public policy, international development, government, the private sector, and institutional relations. The organisation also places emphasis on values including: Inclusiveness Innovation Trust Responsibility These values are reflected in workplace behaviours that include listening and speaking up, collaborating, acting decisively, and simplifying processes to increase impact. For an intern interested in international organisations and development-related work, the environment can provide exposure to how an international financial institution interacts with policymakers, institutions, stakeholders, and other organisations. Purpose of the EBRD Brussels Internship The primary purpose of the position is to provide support to the Brussels team across several areas of work. The intern will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and assist with activities connected to EU policies and initiatives, communications, policy engagement, outreach, events, meetings, administration, and project coordination . Because the role combines policy and communication responsibilities, applicants may benefit from having an interest in both the institutional and public-facing aspects of international development work. The position can therefore provide practical exposure to how policy developments are monitored, analysed, communicated, and incorporated into institutional engagement. Key Responsibilities of the EBRD Intern The selected candidate will be expected to support the team in several areas. 1. Supporting Analysis of EU Policies and Initiatives One of the key responsibilities will involve supporting the analysis of and engagement with European Union policies and initiatives . This means the intern will contribute to the team s understanding of relevant EU developments and help support engagement around policies and initiatives that may be relevant to the EBRD s work. This responsibility could provide valuable exposure to EU policymaking and the relationship between international financial institutions and European institutions. 2. Supporting Communication Activities The intern will also support internal and external communication activities aimed at raising the profile of the EBRD and its EU Representative Office. Communication responsibilities may involve helping the team communicate its activities, priorities, engagements, and work to relevant audiences. This part of the position may be particularly relevant to graduates and early-career professionals with an interest in corporate communications, public affairs, institutional communications, digital communication, or international development communication. 3. Attending Relevant Events The intern will have the opportunity to attend relevant events and report back to management. This responsibility can provide exposure to professional events involving policymakers, institutions, development organisations, financial-sector stakeholders, and other relevant actors. The ability to observe discussions, identify important developments, and communicate key information clearly will therefore be useful in this role. 4. Participating in Meetings The intern may participate in internal and external meetings where appropriate. This provides an opportunity to observe and contribute to professional discussions and gain insight into how an international organisation coordinates its work and engages with external stakeholders. 5. Supporting Policy Engagement and Communication Outreach Another important component of the internship involves supporting the team with both policy engagement and communication outreach . This combines two closely connected areas: understanding and engaging with policy developments while also helping communicate the organisation s work and priorities. Candidates who are comfortable researching information, preparing written materials, communicating professionally, and working with different stakeholders may find these responsibilities particularly relevant. 6. Administrative and Coordination Support The intern will also provide occasional administrative and coordination support for other project activities. Although these tasks may be secondary to the policy and communication responsibilities, they can be important for ensuring that projects and team activities are organised effectively. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail, reliability, and the ability to manage changing priorities can therefore be valuable. Academic and Professional Qualifications The EBRD states that applicants should have a degree with some professional working experience . The vacancy does not specify a single academic discipline in the information provided. Consequently, candidates from different educational backgrounds may potentially be relevant, particularly where their studies and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Relevant academic or professional interests may include areas such as: European studies International relations International development Public policy Political science Economics Finance Communications Corporate communications Public affairs Development studies Business International organisations Applicants should carefully review the official vacancy requirements before applying to determine whether their specific academic and professional background meets the employer s criteria. Professional Experience The vacancy requires candidates to have some professional working experience . The EBRD further notes that experience engaging with EU institutions or international organisations is a plus . This means previous experience in these environments can strengthen an applicant s relevance to the role, although the vacancy presents such experience as an advantage rather than as the stated core qualification. Experience gained through employment, internships, professional assignments, project work, or other relevant professional settings may help demonstrate an applicant s ability to operate in a structured organisational environment. Candidates should focus their application materials on experiences that demonstrate their ability to: Conduct research and analysis Understand policy developments Communicate professionally Work with different stakeholders Prepare or present information Support events and meetings Manage multiple tasks Coordinate activities Work independently Adapt to changing priorities Language Requirements Fluency in English is required for the position. Knowledge of French is an advantage . Because the role is located in Brussels and involves engagement connected to EU institutions and initiatives, language capabilities can be particularly useful when communicating in a multicultural and international environment. Applicants should clearly demonstrate their English-language proficiency and indicate any additional relevant language abilities in their application where appropriate. Knowledge of EU Institutions and Development Policy The EBRD is looking for candidates with knowledge of EU institutions and an understanding of development policy . This requirement is particularly relevant because a substantial part of the internship involves supporting the team s engagement with EU policies and initiatives. Applicants should therefore be familiar with the role and functions of relevant EU institutions and have an understanding of broader development-policy issues. A strong application should demonstrate genuine interest in the policy environment in which the EBRD operates rather than simply listing academic qualifications. Ability to Work Independently The successful candidate should be able to work independently while also understanding when it is appropriate to seek advice. This is an important professional skill in an international organisation where interns may be given individual assignments while also working as part of a wider team. Applicants can demonstrate this capability through examples of situations where they have: Managed assignments independently Met deadlines without constant supervision Taken initiative on projects Identified when additional guidance was needed Communicated challenges promptly Worked responsibly with confidential or important information Ability to Work in a Multicultural Environment The EBRD operates as an international organisation with employees and stakeholders from different professional, cultural, and national backgrounds. The vacancy therefore requires candidates to be able to operate effectively in a multicultural environment with changing priorities . Adaptability, cultural awareness, communication skills, collaboration, professionalism, and openness to different perspectives can all be valuable in such an environment. Applicants should consider highlighting experiences that demonstrate their ability to collaborate with people from different backgrounds and adapt when priorities change. What the EBRD Offers as a Workplace The EBRD describes its workplace as providing varied, stimulating, and engaging work. Employees can interact with experts working across the financial, political, public, and private sectors in the regions where the Bank operates. This type of professional exposure can allow interns to understand how different sectors interact in the context of international development and investment. The organisation also highlights several aspects of its working environment. International and Diverse Professional Environment The EBRD states that it embraces inclusion and celebrates diversity. Its workforce includes people with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. According to the organisation, this diversity contributes fresh ideas, energy, and innovation to its work. For an intern, working in such an environment can provide an opportunity to develop cross-cultural communication and collaboration skills. Hybrid Workplace The EBRD describes its workplace as a hybrid environment , providing flexibility to teams and individuals. The organisation says its approach is based on trust, flexibility, and connectedness. Applicants should nevertheless review the official vacancy and any applicable employment information for the specific working arrangements associated with this internship. Sustainability and Digital Transformation The organisation states that sustainability, equality, and digital transformation are central elements of its environment. These themes are increasingly important across international development and financial institutions, making exposure to them potentially valuable for candidates building careers in related fields. Employee Wellbeing The EBRD also states that its workplace prioritises employee wellbeing and provides a comprehensive suite of competitive benefits. Specific benefits applicable to an intern should be confirmed from the official employment terms and vacancy information. Diversity and Inclusion at the EBRD Diversity is identified by the EBRD as one of its core values. The organisation states that it seeks to ensure that people are treated with respect, given equal opportunities, and able to work in an inclusive environment. The vacancy specifically encourages qualified candidates who are nationals of EBRD member countries to apply regardless of racial, ethnic, religious, or cultural background, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, socioeconomic background, or disability. This is an important point for prospective applicants because eligibility is linked to nationality within the EBRD member-country framework. Candidates should therefore verify that their nationality meets the EBRD s applicable eligibility requirements before submitting an application. Who Should Consider Applying? This internship may be relevant to graduates and early-career professionals who have an academic degree and some professional working experience and who are interested in areas such as: European Union affairs International development International organisations Public policy Development policy Corporate strategy Institutional relations Public affairs Strategic communications International finance Sustainability Government and stakeholder engagement Candidates who have previously engaged with EU institutions or international organisations may have particularly relevant experience because the EBRD identifies this background as an advantage. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants should ensure that their application clearly connects their education and professional experience to the responsibilities described in the vacancy. A strong application can demonstrate: Academic preparation – Clearly state your degree and explain how your academic background relates to the position. Professional experience – Highlight relevant professional experience rather than simply listing previous positions. EU knowledge – Demonstrate your understanding of EU institutions, policies, and initiatives. Development-policy awareness – Show familiarity with development-related issues and explain your interest in the field. Communication skills – Provide evidence of experience supporting internal or external communications. Research and analytical skills – Highlight assignments where you researched, analysed, summarised, or presented information. International experience – If applicable, mention experience working with international organisations, EU institutions, multinational teams, or multicultural stakeholders. Adaptability – Demonstrate that you can manage changing priorities while maintaining the quality of your work. Independent working ability – Give examples of projects or assignments that you successfully handled with limited supervision. Language skills – Clearly indicate your English proficiency and any French-language skills. Important Dates The EBRD published the vacancy on 11 September 2026 . The stated application deadline is 25 September 2026 . Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and should not wait until the final day if they already have the necessary documents prepared. Application Process Interested candidates should apply through the official EBRD careers platform and review the complete vacancy details before submitting their application. The official vacancy should be used to confirm all current requirements, application instructions, and any information concerning the recruitment process. The EBRD also notes that because it receives a high volume of applications, it is unable to provide detailed feedback to candidates who are not shortlisted for further consideration. Working within the EBRD s EU Representative Office can therefore place the intern in an environment where EU policy engagement and international development intersect.
